Zenker Diverticulum

undigested regurgitation in an older man · the barium esophagram before any scope or tube · achalasia and cancer · myotomyIs the regurgitated food undigested, and is the finding in the neck or in the chest?

1Script2Urgent3Differential4Workup5Criteria6Severity7Treatment8Follow-upPractice
1Illness script
Bottom line
  • An older man with undigested food regurgitation, halitosis and a gurgle in the neck has a Zenker diverticulum (pharyngeal diverticulum).
  • Image with a barium esophagram first; passing a scope or nasogastric tube blind can perforate the pouch ⚠︎.
  • Treat with cricopharyngeal myotomy plus a pouch procedure against recurrence; the main complication is aspiration pneumonia.
What it is

Zenker diverticulum (pharyngeal diverticulum): a false, pulsion pouch of mucosa and submucosa pushed out through the posterior wall above the upper esophageal sphincter.

Driver

Cricopharyngeal motor dysfunction: the sphincter muscle fails to relax as the pharynx pushes the bolus down, probably a timing mismatch.

Triggers

Older age

non-modifiable

; male sex

non-modifiable

Chain

Cricopharyngeus does not relax

pressure in the pharynx rises with each swallow

mucosa herniates through Killian triangle, a weak gap just above the cricopharyngeus

the pouch fills with food

regurgitation, halitosis, aspiration

Insights

The pouch sits above the sphincter, so the food it returns is undigested and the finding is in the neck, not the chest.

A blind pouch catches instruments: a scope or tube passed before imaging can enter it and tear through it ⚠︎.

At presentationoropharyngeal dysphagia, undigested regurgitation
As it fillshalitosis, neck gurgle, regurgitation that may come on bending or lying down
At nightregurgitated contents may be aspirated
Rarely, a large pouchsometimes a palpable neck mass, obstruction
2Urgent risks
Act now
FindingAction
Suspected pouch and a scope or feeding tube is plannedImage first with a barium esophagram; a blind scope or nasogastric tube can perforate the pouch ⚠︎.
Fever, productive cough and a lower lobe infiltrate in a patient with a pouchAspiration pneumonia from pouch contents, the main complication (step 8).
Weight loss with progressive dysphagia in a smoker or drinkerEsophageal cancer cannot be missed: endoscopy with biopsy (step 3).
3Differential
Adult dysphagia mimics
DiagnosisDecides itNext best step
AchalasiaSolids and liquids from the start; also regurgitates undigested food; bird beak on esophagram.Confirm with esophageal manometry.
Esophageal cancer, must not missProgressive solid then liquid dysphagia with weight loss; smoking or alcohol (squamous) or long-standing reflux (adenocarcinoma).Upper endoscopy with biopsy.
Oropharyngeal (neurologic) dysphagiaStroke, Parkinson disease or myasthenia; cough or choke as the swallow begins, food or fluid out the nose.Videofluoroscopic swallow study, then speech therapy.
Diffuse esophageal spasmChest pain radiating to the back and neck with intermittent dysphagia; non-peristaltic contractions.Order manometry.
Schatzki ring or peptic strictureIntermittent impaction with meat or bread, no weight loss; distal ring from chronic reflux.Treat with dilation.
4Workup
Clues that change the answer
CluePoints toNext best step
Regurgitates undigested food hours after mealsFood held above the stomach in a pouch or a non-emptying esophagusOrder a barium esophagram.
Gurgling in the neck on swallowing, halitosisZenker diverticulumOrder a barium esophagram before any scope.
Dysphagia to solids and liquids from the startAchalasiaOrder an esophagram, then manometry.
Weight loss with progressive solid-food dysphagiaEsophageal cancerEndoscopy with biopsy.
Coughing at the start of the swallow after a strokeOropharyngeal neurologic dysphagiaOrder a videofluoroscopic swallow study.
Food that may come back on bending or lying down, night coughPouch spilling into the airwayOrder a barium esophagram; treat any pneumonia.

Pause point. The bait: age with dysphagia pulls toward endoscopy for cancer; undigested food with a neck gurgle and stable weight means a pouch, so the esophagram goes first.

5Diagnostic criteria
Where the pouch sits
PouchSiteTied to
ZenkerPosterior, above the upper sphincter (Killian triangle)Pulsion: cricopharyngeal dysfunction
Traction (Rokitansky)MidesophagusPull from mediastinal inflammation, historically tuberculosis
EpiphrenicJust above the diaphragmUsually a motility disorder such as achalasia
6Severity
Pouch and symptoms
FindingAction
Pouch with dysphagia, regurgitation or aspirationSymptomatic: cricopharyngeal myotomy (step 7)
Large pouch, sometimes a palpable neck massSame repair; the size of the defect sets which pouch procedure
Small pouch, no symptomsUsually no specific treatment For esophageal diverticula in general, treatment is usually not required; resection is occasionally needed for large or symptomatic ones. A symptomatic Zenker pouch is treated as in step 7.
7Treatment
1

SymptomaticPouch on the esophagram with symptoms

Cricopharyngeal myotomy plus diverticulectomy, diverticulopexy or diverticulotomy to lower recurrence; the size of the defect sets the choice. Cutting the non-relaxing cricopharyngeus removes the high pressure that pushed the pouch out; the pouch procedure is added against recurrence. In practice: an endoscopic diverticulectomy is an alternative to open diverticulectomy.

2

AvoidBefore or instead of repair

Image before any tube or scope; step 2 owns this rule.

8Follow-up
After diagnosis or repair
SituationDo
Fever, productive cough, lower lobe infiltrateTreat the aspiration pneumonia; it can recur until the pouch is repaired
Symptoms return after repairImage the pouch again with a barium esophagram; recurrence is lower when a pouch procedure was done
Practice
  1. 74 yo M, months of dysphagia, regurgitates undigested food hours after meals, halitosis, gurgling in the neck when he swallows, weight stable → Zenker diverticulum → barium esophagram
  2. 79 yo M with regurgitation of undigested food, halitosis and a gurgling neck → Barium esophagram → a blind scope or tube risks perforating the pouch
  3. 81 yo M with suspected Zenker diverticulum and poor oral intake; the intervention to avoid → Blind nasogastric tube placement → the tube enters the pouch and perforates it
  4. 72 yo M whose esophagram shows a posterior pharyngoesophageal outpouching above the cricopharyngeus → Cricopharyngeal myotomy plus diverticulectomy → the pouch is the symptom, the non-relaxing muscle is the cause
  5. 76 yo M with known Zenker diverticulum, 3 days of fever, productive cough and a right lower lobe infiltrate → Aspiration pneumonia → pooled contents aspirate at night
  6. 46 yo F, dysphagia to solids and liquids from the outset, regurgitation of undigested food, 5 kg weight loss, esophagram with a dilated esophagus tapering to a bird's beak → Achalasia → manometry, then pneumatic dilation or myotomy
  7. 63 yo M, 40 pack-years and daily alcohol, 3 months of progressive solid-food dysphagia now with liquids, 8 kg weight loss → Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma → endoscopy with biopsy
Undigested regurgitation Regurgitated undigested food never reached the stomach; a pouch or a non-emptying esophagus held it. With a neck finding it is a Zenker pouch; with dysphagia to liquids from day one it is achalasia. In both, the first study is the esophagram. Endoscopy comes first only with an alarm feature for cancer (weight loss, smoking, progressive solid dysphagia) and no neck finding.
Pearls Zenker is a false (pulsion) diverticulum: mucosa and submucosa herniate through the posterior wall at Killian triangle, between the thyropharyngeal and cricopharyngeal parts of the inferior pharyngeal constrictor · the mechanism is cricopharyngeal motor dysfunction (diminished relaxation), not structural weakness alone · halitosis comes from food decaying in the pouch · the main complication is aspiration pneumonia · treatment is cricopharyngeal myotomy plus a pouch procedure (diverticulectomy, diverticulopexy or diverticulotomy), chosen by the size of the defect
The decision point Ask: is the regurgitated food undigested, and is the finding in the neck or in the chest?
Transferable rule When the diagnosis implies a blind pouch or cavity the instrument cannot see, image it before instrumenting it: esophagram before endoscopy in Zenker, as with ultrasound before aspirating a hip effusion.
Sequencing trapUpper endoscopy is ordered too early; a blind scope can perforate the pouch that the esophagram would have shown.
Salient decoyWeight loss and age suggest cancer, but undigested regurgitation with a neck gurgle indicates a pouch, and the esophagram evaluates both.
Class-vs-memberManometry evaluates motility disorders such as achalasia, not a pharyngeal pouch.
